cell.notes: Massing reads as a single heavy stone block taller than wide, which honors the guard-block brief — but the silhouette is lumpy and the crown dissolves into an irregular, partly-collapsed roof rather than a clean steep gable, so the base→middle→crown rhythm never resolves (competent proportion at best). Palette is disciplined near-monochrome stone grey with a dark band and a strip of warm brown at the base; restrained but unremarkable, and the brown reads as an unfinished plinth rather than a deliberate arch/door accent, so color stays competent. Detail is the weakest dimension: the surface is a homogeneous grey field of texture noise with no legible relief — no voussoir ring, no slit windows, no buttress pilasters articulate the walls; it is flat fields plus aliasing. Fidelity suffers most from the gate: the one feature that should name the building — a chunky arched passage tunnelling the base — is not legible; the front shows only a rectangular notch that reads as a missing chunk, not an arch. Without a clear entrance or gable read it lands as a generic stone blob, not a recognizable gatehouse. Overall weak: a plausible stone mass that fails to deliver its two naming features (arch + peaked gable) and offers no articulated surface.
